updates.title: OMD headline Rochdale tonight with Peter Hook & The Light and A Certain Ratio
updates.body:
Tonight, synth-pop icons Orchestral Manoeuvres in the Dark (OMD) perform a headline show alongside special guests Peter Hook & The Light and A Certain Ratio.

With a career spanning more than four decades, more than 40 million records sold worldwide and 18 Top 40 hits, OMD are one of Britain's best-loved and most influential pop groups. In 1979, they famously recorded the single 'Electricity' at Cargo Studios in Rochdale. Genre-defining hits followed, including Enola Gay, Maid of Orleans, Souvenir and If You Leave, helping shape the musical landscape of the 1980s.

Following their 40th anniversary celebrations, OMD returned in 2023 with Bauhaus Staircase, their first studio album in six years. The record received widespread critical acclaim and marked a creative resurgence for the band, who went on to play their biggest UK tour, culminating in their largest London show to date at The O2.

OMD's live shows are known for energy, nostalgia and synth-driven brilliance, and the band are promising a night of dancing and timeless hits as they return to Rochdale to headline one of the north's most spectacular heritage venues.

Joining OMD are Peter Hook & The Light, the post-punk band fronted by Joy Division and New Order co-founder Peter Hook, who also recorded at Cargo Studios, further cementing Rochdale's role in the post-punk and electronic music scene. They are set to play a career-spanning set featuring seminal tracks from the back catalogues of Joy Division and New Order.

Opening the evening will be Manchester post-punk/funk band A Certain Ratio. Formed in the late 1970s and signed to Tony Wilson's Factory Records, they too recorded at Cargo Studios in Rochdale.

Staged in partnership with Rochdale Borough Council and Rochdale Development Agency, the special show is part of Rochdale Music Stories — a campaign launched in 2025 as part of the town's year as Greater Manchester Town of Culture, celebrating Rochdale's longstanding influence on British music while promoting the next wave of talent.

updates.title: La Mancha gets festival weekend under way with tapas before the tunes
updates.body:
La Mancha is getting into the Feel Good Festival spirit ahead of the weekend, inviting festival-goers to make the popular Rochdale town-centre restaurant their first stop before heading to the music.

The Spanish restaurant is promoting tapas, cocktails and sangria for visitors looking to eat and drink before the festival action, with its town-centre location making it a convenient pre-event stop.

The festival weekend brings a major line-up into Rochdale, and town-centre bars and restaurants are preparing for increased footfall as visitors arrive for the live music and wider entertainment programme.

La Mancha is encouraging customers planning to visit over the festival weekend to book a table in advance.

updates.title: Welcome to our live festival coverage
updates.body:
Rochdale's biggest weekend of the year is here, and we'll be posting updates on this page throughout — set times as they're confirmed, what's happening around the town centre, and anything you need to know before heading in.

The main event is tomorrow, Saturday 8 August: the festival opens at 11.30am, with BRIT Award winner Gabrielle headlining the main stage in Town Hall Square, joined on the bill by Ash, Starsailor and more, alongside the Food and Drink Village and live music in venues across the town centre. Tonight's ticketed warm-up show gets the weekend under way.

For the full rundown of the bill, entry rules, travel and accessibility, read our complete festival guide linked at the top of this page.
